INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, so a later pass need not re-derive: solving the Markov system tr_M(1)=1, tr_M(sigma)=z, tr_M(sigma_1 sigma_2)=z^2 against the H_3(q) characters under convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1)) gives EXACTLY y = ((q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, q^2/(q^2+1)^2, 0), which is precisely the block's [4]_q/[2]_q^3, 1/[2]_q^2, 0 (the two forms are algebraically identical via [2]_q = (q^2+1)/q, [4]_q = (q^4+1)(q^2+1)/q^3) -- and numerically 0.5054042, 0.2472979, 0. The block's C vector (0.4154, 0.2809, 0.0227) is also exactly what convention C yields. z(q_0) = 0.499320, 1.2% below 0.5054042 (computed 1.204%); ~20% against 0.4154 (computed 20.2%); sqrt(q_0) = 1.05356 vs (1+q_0)/2 = 1.05499. All correct. ONE MINOR internal inconsistency: y_(2,1)(q_0) is given as '~0.001' in the sanity-check paragraph and '~0.0007' two paragraphs later; the true value is 0.000680.
